stories.headline: Nvidia delays next-gen Kyber NVL144 AI rack by 12+ months to 2028 on PCB snags

key_facts.fact: Nvidia's Kyber rack-scale architecture, designed to house its 2027 Rubin Ultra chips, has been delayed by more than 12 months to 2028, according to research firm SemiAnalysis in a post published Monday July 6.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA's next marquee product — the Kyber rack-scale architecture designed to house its 2027 Rubin Ultra chips — has been delayed by more than 12 months to 2028, according to research firm SemiAnalysis, the latest in a string of reported setbacks.

key_facts.fact: The setback stems from difficulty manufacturing a specialized multi-layer PCB 'midplane' at the heart of the system, which SemiAnalysis said 'remains challenging from a manufacturability standpoint.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Kyber NVL144 rack architecture has been delayed to 2028 as the PCB midplane remains challenging from a manufacturability standpoint," the firm said, referring to a specialized, multi-layer printed circuit board.

key_facts.fact: The midplane consists of 78 layers and is highly prone to defects; the larger NVL576 configuration (576 GPUs) is also experiencing manufacturing issues.
key_facts.excerpt: This 'midplane' consists of 78 layers and is highly prone to defects. The larger NVL576, which, as the name suggests, is equipped with 576 GPUs, is also experiencing manufacturing issues.

key_facts.fact: Kyber packs 144 of Nvidia's most powerful chips into a single rack unit and had been slated to debut with the Vera Rubin Ultra system in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Kyber is a server cabinet that packs 144 of Nvidia's most powerful chips into a single unit... had been slated to debut with Vera Rubin Ultra, Nvidia's next-generation rack-scale system, in 2027.

key_facts.fact: A backup plan to bolt two current-generation racks together (NVL72x2) has been scrapped after cloud service providers and hyperscalers rejected the design as awkward and costly to operate.
key_facts.excerpt: A backup plan — bolting two of Nvidia's current-generation racks together for similar power — has also been scrapped after cloud customers rejected the design as awkward and costly to operate.

stories.headline: SK Hynix launches ~$28B US share sale for Nasdaq listing, draws $7B in interest

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix on Monday July 6 launched a US share sale to raise 43 trillion won (about $28.07 billion), drawing indications of interest for up to $7 billion from major investors.
key_facts.excerpt: South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix on Monday launched a U.S. share sale to raise 43 trillion won ($28.07 billion) and drew indications of interest for up to $7 billion from major investors.

key_facts.fact: The company is issuing up to 17,790,000 new common shares, about 2.50% of its outstanding shares, and intends to list the ADSs on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol 'SKHY.'
key_facts.excerpt: the maximum number of new common shares to be issued in connection with this offering is 17,790,000 shares, representing approximately 2.50% of our total issued and outstanding common shares... We intend to apply to list the ADSs on the Nasdaq Global Select Market (the 'Nasdaq') under the symbol 'SKHY.'

key_facts.fact: At roughly $28-29 billion the deal may be the biggest-ever first-time share sale by a foreign company, surpassing Alibaba's $21.8 billion New York debut in 2014.
key_facts.excerpt: This week's $29 billion US stock-market listing for SK Hynix Inc. may be the biggest-ever first-time share sale by a foreign company.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix plans to list its ADRs on the Nasdaq on July 10, with proceeds funding a chip factory, an advanced packaging fab in South Korea, and chipmaking equipment such as an EUV scanner.
key_facts.excerpt: ADRs will be priced at 255,500 won apiece, and listed on the Nasdaq on July 10... the proceeds from the stock sale will be used to construct a chip factory, an advanced packaging fab in South Korea and to buy chipmaking equipment, such as an extreme ultraviolet scanner (EUV).

key_facts.fact: BofA Securities, Citigroup Global Markets, Goldman Sachs and JP Morgan Securities are managing the offering.
key_facts.excerpt: BofA Securities, Citigroup Global Markets, Goldman Sachs and JP Morgan Securities are managing the offering, SK Hynix said.

stories.headline: China's Biren raises ~$892M in H-share placement to scale GPU production

key_facts.fact: Shanghai-based AI chipmaker Biren Technology announced its first placement on Monday July 6, issuing 153 million new H shares at HK$46.2 each to raise nearly HK$7.07 billion (about $892.5 million) in gross proceeds.
key_facts.excerpt: Biren Technology (6082) announced its first plaing plan on Monday to seize current development opportunities by issuing 153 million new H shares at HK$46.2 each, raising nearly HK$7.07 billion in gross proceeds.

key_facts.fact: The placement price represents a discount of about 9.94% to the prior Friday's close and accounts for roughly 11.3% of the enlarged H share capital.
key_facts.excerpt: The placement represents a discount of approximately 9.94 percent to last Friday's closing price. It accounts for about 12.74 percent of the issued H shares and approximately 11.3 percent of the enlarged H share capital.

key_facts.fact: About 60% of net proceeds will accelerate commercialization and production of next-generation products, 20% for R&D, 10% for strategic investments and acquisitions, and 10% for working capital.
key_facts.excerpt: about 60 percent will be used to accelerate the commercialization and production of next-generation products; about 10 percent for strategic investments and acquisitions; and about 10 percent for working capital and general corporate purposes.

key_facts.fact: Biren, which is positioning to challenge Nvidia, listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in early January 2026, and its stock is up more than 150% since the IPO.
key_facts.excerpt: Shanghai-based AI chipmaker Biren raises ~$892.5M in a new share sale to boost GPU production; Biren's stock is up 150%+ since its January Hong Kong IPO.

key_facts.fact: Biren said additional funding needs arose since its listing due to accelerated market adoption, expanded pre-research programs and greater near-term commercialization commitments that were not fully anticipated at the time of the IPO.
key_facts.excerpt: since its listing, the company has identified additional funding needs due to accelerated market adoption, expansion of pre-research programs, increased customer engagement and validation activities, and greater near-term commercialization and supply chain commitments.

stories.headline: Camera-free smart-glasses maker Even Realities raises $150M at $1B valuation

key_facts.fact: Even Realities, a three-year-old Shenzhen-headquartered startup, raised $150 million in a pre-Series B round led by Meituan and previous backer Tencent, valuing the company at $1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Even Realities, a three-year-old Shenzhen-headquartered startup, has raised $150 million in a pre-Series B round led by Meituan and previous backer Tencent; the round valued the startup at $1 billion valuation.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2023 by former Apple engineers, the company makes camera-free, display-first smart glasses that beam information into the wearer's line of sight, positioning against camera-equipped rivals like Meta's Ray-Bans on privacy grounds.
key_facts.excerpt: This Shenzhen-based startup makes smart glasses without cameras, putting it in direct competition with Meta's Ray-Ban models, which have raised privacy concerns.

key_facts.fact: More than half of Even Realities' users and about 80% of its developer community are based in the United States.
key_facts.excerpt: More than half of its users and about 80% of its developer community are based in the United States, the company said.

key_facts.fact: The round lifts total funding above $160 million; earlier investors include Hillhouse, Sequoia China and Northern Light Venture Capital, and the company's first product, the G1, launched in 2024 with waveguide optics.
key_facts.excerpt: Previous investors in Even Realities are Hillhouse, Sequoia China, and Northern Light Venture Capital. The first product, the G1, was launched in 2024 as the lightest smart glasses on the market with waveguide optics.

stories.headline: Swiss photonics startup Aylight raises 4.5M euros for AI data-center optical interconnects

key_facts.fact: Zurich-based deeptech startup Aylight closed a 4.5 million euro pre-seed round to develop chip-scale multiwavelength lasers for AI data-center optical interconnects and FMCW sensing.
key_facts.excerpt: Swiss photonics startup Aylight has raised 4.5 million euros in a pre-seed funding round to support the development of its chip-scale multiwavelength laser technology.

key_facts.fact: The round was co-led by Elaia and Swisscom Ventures, with participation from Verve Ventures and Plug and Play.
key_facts.excerpt: The round was co-led by Elaia and Swisscom Ventures, with participation from Verve Ventures and Plug and Play.

key_facts.fact: Aylight's technology generates multiple precisely spaced wavelengths from a single chip, reducing the need for multiple discrete lasers, and is designed to be manufactured on existing semiconductor photonics foundries.
key_facts.excerpt: Its technology generates multiple precisely spaced wavelengths from a single chip, reducing the need for multiple discrete lasers in optical communication systems... designed to be manufactured using existing semiconductor photonics foundries.

key_facts.fact: Aylight was founded in 2025 by Bahareh Marzban and Dmitry Kazakov following research at ETH Zurich; the funding will support its first semiconductor-foundry prototypes.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2025 by Bahareh Marzban and Dmitry Kazakov following research at ETH Zurich, Aylight develops chip-scale multiwavelength lasers for AI data-centre optical interconnects.

sources.title: Aylight closes 4.5M euro pre-seed round to advance optical interconnect technology
